text:
morgan: FYI — spike in prefix cache misses on r10a (us-west-2). KV backend QPS ~4x baseline, tail 99.9 latency -> 2.1s. Observed increased 504s from model-serving frontends. Rolling revert of new prefix-normalization started (will update).
infra-bot: [ALERT] kv-cache-service: error-rate 3.9% threshold breached, autoscale triggered. https://ops/alerts/1234
ben: any idea what triggered it? recent deploys to runtime/kv-keying yesterday? @carol
carol: pushed a change to prefix hashing and canonicalization at 02:10 UTC that tightened key scope (fewer equivalent keys) — but I forgot to preserve legacy fallback salt. suspect churn in keyspace -> low hit reuse -> backend QPS spike.
dave: quick profiling: flame CPU at 02:20 shows extra time in kernel selection path because more short-lived KV misses -> more cache fills -> heavier batching overhead. key: 'select_kernel_for_shard' called ~3x more than baseline.
carol: logs excerpt:
```
[02:18:14] kv-miss: key=prefix:usr:abcd1234 -> ns=256
[02:18:14] fill_start shard=12
[02:18:14] fill_done ttl=60ms
```
priya: ran a hit-rate query, pre-change hitrate ~78%, current ~22% for affected prefix groups (user-facing conversational endpoints). Query used:
```
SELECT prefix, count(*) as q, SUM(hit) / COUNT(*) as hr FROM cache_metrics WHERE hour=... GROUP BY prefix ORDER BY q DESC LIMIT 20
```
ben: urgent next steps: 1) emergency-disable key-normalizer (in progress) 2) temporarily raise per-shard batching window to 10ms to absorb fill churn 3) throttle frontend QPS to backend via token bucket. anyone object?
morgan: +1 do them all, but raising batching window may hurt p50 for small requests — acceptable for now.
infra-bot: deploy: runtime/patch-rollback started by dave @ 02:34 UTC
dave: rollback complete at 02:38. I've also increased batching window in config: `batch.max_delay_ms=10` and enabled provisional backpressure against KV fetches.
carol: after rollback, hit-rate climbing back to ~65% in 10m. kernel-selection CPU down ~30%. still seeing elevated tail but much improved.
priya: long term: propose keying migration plan: server-side stable canonicalization with deterministic salt + gradual rehashing (rolling rekey over shards), plus warmup strategy: slow prefetch with leaky-bucket (max 50 fills/s per shard) and jittered TTL to avoid synchronization.
ben: also add metrics: per-prefix cardinality (unique keys/time) + prefetch success ratio to detect regressing key entropy early.
morgan: opened follow-up RFC: https://go/rfcs/kv-keying-solidify. keep monitoring, will update this thread. :thumbsup:
